artists.biography:
The All Seeing I were an English electronic music group from Sheffield, comprising Dean Honer, Jason Buckle and DJ Parrot (real name Richard Barratt). They released their first single "I Walk" in 1997, but it was not until the year after that they gained mainstream commercial success with the song "Beat Goes On", a remixed cover of the Sonny Bono song, using the all-female vocals from Buddy Rich's version). 
Their work was something of a Sheffield collective, and the trio worked with artists from the city including Tony Christie, Jarvis Cocker, Philip Oakey, Babybird and many others. Their regular live vocalist was Bozz, who later went on to form electronica duo Hiem. 
All Seeing I were asked in November 1998 to produce a cover of "Beat Goes On" for Britney Spears's debut album ...Baby One More Time. They have also remixed a variety of artists, including Pulp. 
Dean Honer also fronts the similarly styled group, I Monster. 
Buckle went on to be a part-time member of Fat Truckers and formed Relaxed Muscle with Jarvis Cocker. He also has a brief cameo as one of the Weird Sisters rock band in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, along with Cocker, Pulp's Steve Mackey, Steve Claydon of Add N to (X), and Phil Selway and Jonny Greenwood of Radiohead. 
Barratt was part of the duo Sweet Exorcist with Richard H. Kirk (of Cabaret Voltaire fame).

Pickled Eggs & Sherbet is the sole studio album by Sheffield-based electronic trio The All Seeing I, released in 1999 on London Records. The group, comprising Dean Honer (keyboards, programming, production), Jason Buckle (guitars, bass, production), and Richard Barrett, also known as DJ Parrot (drums, programming, production), crafted a record that blended big beat, electronic, and trip hop influences characteristic of late-1990s British electronic music. The album showcased Honer's production prowess, a skill he would later apply to subsequent projects including I Monster, The Moonlandingz, and Add N To (X).

The album's commercial appeal was bolstered by notable guest vocalists and songwriting contributions. "Walk Like a Panther," featuring crooner Tony Christie and written by Pulp's Jarvis Cocker, became one of the project's signature tracks, while "1st Man in Space" featured The Human League's Philip Oakey. Other notable collaborators included Stephen Jones on "Plastic Diamond," and the album opened with the track "I Walk," which had previously appeared as the band's debut single in 1997. The album reached No. 45 on the UK Albums Chart, establishing a modest but respectable commercial foothold.

Despite being the group's only album release, Pickled Eggs & Sherbet has maintained cultural relevance, particularly after "Beat Goes On" experienced a resurgence as a viral hit in 2022. The album's eclectic tracklist and star-studded guest appearances reflected the collaborative spirit of the late-1990s British electronic scene, though the project ultimately remained a singular statement rather than the foundation for an ongoing recording career.
